note: Names follow the default tax rates in Xero's AU and UK organisations. QuickBooks Online uses different labels for the same treatments (for example 'GST' and 'GST free' in AU, '20.0% S' and '0.0% Z' in the UK). The names were not checked against a live file; check the tax rates list in your own organisation.

AU.name: GST on Income
AU.useFor: Most sales of goods and services in Australia.

AU.name: GST Free Income
AU.reportsIn: G1 and G3 (exports go in G2)
AU.useFor: GST-free sales: most basic food, some health and education, exports.

AU.name: Input Taxed
AU.reportsIn: G1 and G4 on a sale; no GST credit on a purchase
AU.useFor: Financial supplies, residential rent. No GST charged and no GST credit claimable on related purchases.

AU.name: GST on Expenses
AU.useFor: Everyday business purchases from a GST-registered supplier with a tax invoice.

AU.name: GST on Capital
AU.useFor: Purchases of capital items (equipment, vehicles) with GST.

AU.name: GST Free Expenses
AU.reportsIn: G11 (or G10 for capital) with no 1B
AU.useFor: Purchases with no GST: bank fees, some insurance and stamp duty, unregistered suppliers, overseas services.

AU.name: BAS Excluded
AU.useFor: Wages, super, PAYG, loans, transfers between accounts, owner drawings and capital, income tax, dividends.

AU.name: GST on Imports
AU.reportsIn: 1B (GST paid to Customs on imported goods)
AU.useFor: The GST line of an import declaration, paid to the Department of Home Affairs, not to the supplier.

UK.name: 20% (VAT on Income)
UK.useFor: Most sales of goods and services.

UK.name: 5% (VAT on Income)
UK.useFor: Reduced-rate sales such as domestic fuel and power, children's car seats.

UK.name: Zero Rated Income
UK.useFor: Zero-rated sales: most food, books, children's clothes, exports of goods.

UK.name: Exempt Income
UK.useFor: Exempt sales: insurance, finance, most residential rent, some education and health.

UK.name: 20% (VAT on Expenses)
UK.useFor: Most business purchases from a VAT-registered supplier with a VAT invoice.

UK.name: 5% (VAT on Expenses)
UK.useFor: Reduced-rate purchases such as business energy below the de minimis.

UK.name: Zero Rated Expenses
UK.useFor: Zero-rated purchases: most food, books, public transport fares.

UK.name: Exempt Expenses
UK.useFor: Exempt purchases: insurance premiums, bank interest, postage stamps (Royal Mail).

UK.name: No VAT
UK.useFor: Outside the scope: wages, PAYE and NIC, VAT payments, dividends, loans, transfers, MOT certificates, statutory fees.

UK.name: Domestic Reverse Charge @ 20% (VAT on Expenses)
UK.useFor: Construction services reported under CIS, received from a VAT-registered subcontractor, when you are not the end user.

UK.name: Domestic Reverse Charge @ 20% (VAT on Income)
UK.useFor: Your own construction sales to a VAT-registered contractor who is not the end user: the invoice says 'reverse charge' and shows no VAT to pay.
